sents.t: On Sunday, Rosa invited me for dinner.
“You’ve been quiet all week,” she said.
“Tell me.”
I told her everything: the job, the salary, the dream, and my fear of leaving.
Rosa poured two cups of tea.
“When I was young, I used to live in Texas,” she said.
“I had a good job. But my mother got sick, so I came back to Oakville. For years, I used to wonder about that life.”
“Do you regret it?”
“Not for one day,” she said.
“But that was my choice, Sam. Not yours. What matters most to you?”
That night, I made two lists.
Chicago: my dream job, more money, Emma, a big city.
Oakville: Lily, Rosa, Max, my team, the podcast, the people who became my family.
When I looked at the lists, my decision was easy.
I finally knew what home meant.
On Monday, I called Harbor Books and explained that I couldn’t move.
There was a long pause.
Then the editor surprised me.
“What if you worked for us part-time, from Oakville? You could translate two books a year and visit Chicago once a month.”
I said yes immediately and ran to Maple Café to tell Lily.
She hugged me so hard that we both fell into a chair, laughing.
